citations.assessment: Checked the warning, offense, ben Temalyon scene, collective tearing of the decree and the curtain. Rashi on Yoma explicitly attributes the cure and handling of the decree to Elazar.
Rashi on Meilah refers details of illness and cure to an aggadah. The stated sailor detail remains held, and the emperor’s daughter calls for Shimon in this commentary.
The named chain includes Yose the Galilean between Yose ben Dormaskit and Yochanan ben Nuri. The direct Tosefta comparison lacks that intermediary.
Names Elazar as seeing the curtain and blood drops in Rome. A second report on the same daf describes a different offering.
Rashi explicitly attributes the rescue of the king’s daughter, tearing of the decree and the observation of the Temple vessels to Elazar.
Eliezer son of Rabbi Yose reports seeing the gold plate and its single-line inscription in Rome.
Yose relates his son’s calculation of how few booths were needed.
The gloss gives the manner of speech and explains the eruv distance calculation.
Yose quotes his son on who first recited Hallel and distinguishes the rival David attribution.
The chain runs from Eliezer son of Yose through Yose son of Dormaskit directly to Yochanan ben Nuri. The Bavli names Yose the Galilean as an additional intermediary.
The named speaker directly recalls entering Alexandria and speaking there with an elder.
The Tosefta explicitly gives his ruling in Rome about an aqueduct opening affecting a ritual bath. The exact Niddah locator remains held.
Both men appear together in the Yavneh assembly along with Shimon.
The baraita explicitly gives both Elazar and Yose bar Yehudah as transmitters of Zekharyah on maternal inheritance.
